title: Traditional Mysuru Paak (Sample Heritage Sweet)
summary: A traditional Karnataka melt-in-mouth confection prepared from sieved gram flour, hot clarified butter (ghee), and one-string sugar syrup. (NOTE: This is a synthetic sample created by the project maintainer for testing and demonstration, not recorded from a living individual).

ingredients_or_materials.name: Besan (Bengal gram flour / ಕಡಲೆ ಹಿಟ್ಟು)
ingredients_or_materials.note: Sieved twice through a fine mesh sieve to eliminate lumps

ingredients_or_materials.name: Pure Desi Ghee (Clarified butter / ತುಪ್ಪ)
ingredients_or_materials.note: Kept gently heated and melted in a side saucepan throughout preparation

ingredients_or_materials.name: Sugar (Granulated cane sugar / ಸಕ್ಕರೆ)
ingredients_or_materials.note: Refined white or raw cane sugar

ingredients_or_materials.name: Water
ingredients_or_materials.note: Just sufficient to submerge and dissolve the sugar

tools: Heavy-bottomed iron or brass kadai (deep frying pan)
Small sauce pan with ladle (for continuous hot ghee addition)
Greased high-rimmed metal tray or rectangular tin
Straight-edge pastry knife for scoring warm squares

steps.instruction: Sieve the gram flour twice into a wide bowl. Fold in two tablespoons of warm melted ghee to create a loose, clump-free paste.
steps.spoken_tip: Rubbing warm ghee into the dry flour before it touches the boiling syrup stops lumps from ever forming in the kadai.

steps.instruction: In a heavy-bottomed kadai over medium heat, dissolve two cups of sugar in half a cup of water and boil until one-string consistency (oru kambi padam) is achieved.
steps.spoken_tip: Dip your ladle, let a drop cool slightly, and test between thumb and forefinger—it must pull into a continuous thin single string before you add the flour.

steps.instruction: Lower the flame to low and pour the gram flour paste into the bubbling syrup in a steady stream, stirring continuously in one direction with a wooden spatula.
steps.spoken_tip: Keep the ladle moving along the bottom of the pan so the gram flour cooks evenly without catching or scorching.

steps.instruction: Ladle in boiling hot ghee one ladle at a time. Stir continuously until the mixture absorbs the ghee completely before ladling in the next portion.
steps.spoken_tip: The ghee must be hot when added. If you ladle cold ghee into the mixture, the sugar will seize and you lose the porous structure.

steps.instruction: Watch for the froth: when the entire mass turns light, expands with honeycomb-like air pockets, and separates cleanly from the pan edges, immediately invert it into the greased tin.
steps.spoken_tip: Never pat or press the top down with your spoon. Let the trapped air bubbles remain inside for the classic porous honeycomb texture.

steps.instruction: Allow the poured sweet to settle undisturbed for 10 minutes until warm, then score into diamond or square blocks with a warm, oiled blade.
steps.spoken_tip: Cut while it is still warm to the touch. Once it cools completely, it hardens and will shatter into irregular crumbs.

tips: Maintain the ghee on low simmer on the back burner throughout the entire cooking process.
Do not compress the sweet after pouring into the tin; natural aeration gives Mysore Pak its iconic soft honeycomb texture.
safety_notes: Hot molten sugar syrup and boiling ghee reach temperatures above 130°C and cause severe burns; use long wooden utensils and beware of splattering when ladling hot ghee.
Do not handle the poured sweet with bare hands until it has rested for at least 15 minutes.

uncertain_items.reason: Mentioned as an optional variation in speech, but not shown among the measured ingredients.
Speaker mentions 'mildly roasted' but flour color varies depending on regional pulses.
